title: AdCodicem.Pdf corpus manifest
description: Every document of the test corpus, what the tests must observe on it, and where it comes from (docs/corpus.md). Also the shape of tests/corpus/private.json. CorpusManifestSchemaTests holds the manifest to this schema, and this schema to the model in tests/AdCodicem.Pdf.TestSupport/Corpus.cs and to the library's codes.

producers.description: The versions of the producers build_corpus.py last ran, by name.

document.description: One corpus document. expect is what the tests assert; readerLimits how it is opened; the rest is provenance.

file.description: The document's path under tests/corpus: documents/ for our own, vendor/ for a committed third party's, remote/ for one fetched on demand (ADR 32), private/ in private.json.

builtBy.description: The script that writes the file, when one does; build_corpus.py replaces only its own entries.

title.description: What the document is, in our own words.

useCase.description: What the document is, not which feature it exercises (docs/corpus.md, use-case categories).

producer.description: The software that wrote the file, with its version when known.

origin.description: generated here, contributed as it is, derived from another document, or remote: fetched on demand, never committed (ADR 32).

licence.description: Under what terms the document is used; for a remote one, why it is remote rather than vendored.

features.description: What the document exercises, as short tags; each tag once.

expectation.description: What the tests must observe on the document, each established by an independent tool or from the file itself, never by our own code.

pages.description: The page count an independent tool establishes (qpdf --show-npages), or null when it recovers nothing.

clean.description: Whether the file is well formed: a clean document earns no repair and no warning from the reader.

indexRebuilt.description: Whether the reader must rebuild the cross-reference index.

catalogRecoverable.description: Only for a file with no catalogue at all, which the reader must open and hand back none; every other entry leaves the field out.

requiredDiagnostics.description: Diagnostic codes the reader must report (PdfDiagnosticCodes).

findings.description: The validation rules that report on the document under the default profile (PdfValidationRuleIds) — exactly these; left out, none.

refereeCheckSucceeds.description: Whether qpdf --check finds nothing wrong, recorded by build_corpus.py from the very command the integration tests run.

password.description: The password that opens it; empty for an owner password alone.

formFields.description: Interactive form fields the document declares (M11).

hasExtractableText.description: False for an image-only document, which must report no text rather than noise (M10).

claimsConformance.description: The conformance level the document claims, such as PDF/A-3b.

conformanceValid.description: Whether veraPDF upholds the claimed level (M12).

unsupported.description: Why the library cannot yet meet the expectations, starting with the milestone or debt row that will, such as 'M2: …': the acceptance tests skip the document with this reason.

readerLimits.description: The reader limits a valid document that exceeds a default is opened with (ADR 34): each named after a property of PdfReaderLimits, and each must raise its default.

maxDecodedStreamLength.description: What one stream may decode to, in bytes.

maxObjectLength.description: The longest object, the data of a stream aside, in bytes.

maxXRefSectionLength.description: The longest classic cross-reference section, in bytes.

maxXRefSectionCount.description: The most cross-reference sections in a chain.

source.description: Where a third party's file was retrieved, so provenance is checkable without trusting the repository; mandatory for a remote document, which fetch_remote.py downloads and verifies.

url.description: Where the bytes are published — or the archive they are a member of (ADR 33). A committed file taken out of an archive may name its member after the URL, as '(member name.pdf)'; a remote one never, since fetch_remote.py downloads the URL as it stands.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the document's bytes as published.

retrieved.description: When it was retrieved, as YYYY-MM-DD.

landingPage.description: The page that presents it, or a persistent identifier such as a DOI.

archive.description: The pinned archive a remote document is a member of (ADR 33): the download is checked against this pin, the member against the document's.

member.description: The member's path inside the archive: relative, POSIX, with no control character and no empty, '.' or '..' segment.
